name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,321

clue.text: Blog about West overwhelmed by frightful climate change

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned around and rearranged, so the four letters of blog are reordered
something overwhelmed is swamped and surrounded, so the compass letter sits inside the adjective

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
frightful means alarming
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A blog post about the West being swamped by terrifying climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers only the blog word; the compass letter then sits inside the adjective, and the two halves join.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming is the rise in Earth's temperatures, the best-known form of climate change.

clue.text: General appearance of men in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for men is taken by its sound

blocks.note: guys is an informal word for men

explanation.surface: Someone judging the overall look of the men trying out at an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or manner of presentation, often a disguise.

clue.text: Coppers or pound note?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for the police
second meaning, read literally: an aged banknote, as the British pound note was withdrawn in 1988

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests copper coins, setting up a money theme; it is actually British slang for police officers, known collectively as the Old Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bill is British slang for the police, and a pound note is literally an old bill of currency.

clue.text: Handsome man not half in trouble

indicators.note: only half of the name survives, the back half being dropped

blocks.note: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, stands for any handsome man

explanation.surface: A good-looking man who is in a lot of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: ADONIS has six letters; keeping the first three gives ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in 'much ado about nothing', a mild form of trouble.

clue.text: Ride Raleigh, perhaps, around Zambia

indicators.note: the explorer's first name is placed around the country letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: Sir Walter Raleigh, the Elizabethan explorer, is one example of a Walter
Z is Zambia's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: Cycling a Raleigh bicycle across Zambia.
explanation.walkthrough: Raleigh looks like the bicycle brand, making 'Ride' a verb; it is Sir Walter Raleigh, and 'Ride' is a noun, a fairground attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A waltzer is a fairground ride whose cars spin as they travel round an undulating track.

clue.text: Love to wear a mini-dress for a change? This gains one further acceptance

indicators.note: making a change to the dress and its letters lets them be put in a fresh order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: Someone in love tries on a mini-dress for a change, and that wins them a second welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: O is put into the mini-dress letters and the whole lot rearranged. The definition is the whole second sentence: this word names something that gets one accepted again.
explanation.definitionFit: Readmission is being admitted again, for instance back into a club or hospital, so a further acceptance.

clue.text: One politician didn't tell the truth, it is suggested

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
to lie is to not tell the truth

explanation.surface: A rumour that some politician has been dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied means hinted at without being said outright, the same as suggested.

clue.text: To increase speed, athlete's one who moves arms impermissibly

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it hard to speed up
a runner is one kind of athlete

explanation.surface: A sprinter picking up pace, pumping their arms in a way the rules forbid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moves arms' looks like an athlete's running style; here arms are weapons being smuggled.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunrunner smuggles firearms illegally, so moves weapons without permission.

clue.text: Violent, dirty tackle reported in game

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the tackle word counts by its sound

blocks.note: wild can mean violent and uncontrolled
a dirty tackle in football is a foul

explanation.surface: A referee's report of a nasty, violent foul during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the match itself; it means wild animals and birds hunted for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildfowl are ducks, geese and similar birds shot by hunters, which count as game.

clue.text: Pop over and write down "Hang on!"

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word for father reads the other way

blocks.note: pop and pa are both informal words for father
to pen is to write
D is the standard abbreviation for down

explanation.surface: A note to drop by and jot down the instruction to wait a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang on!' reads as 'wait'; taken literally it means attach something.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to add or attach something at the end, literally to hang it on.

clue.text: Indian city with no hospital or place to buy food

indicators.note: 'with no' says a letter is taken away from the city's name

blocks.note: Delhi is India's capital territory
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A city in India without a hospital or anywhere to get food.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the H from DELHI leaves DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: State, without question, there's a zombie shambling beside motorway

indicators.note: a shambling walk is clumsy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled
'without' in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the question symbol
placed beside means set next to, joining the motorway letter on at the front

blocks.note: M is the prefix of British motorway names, as in the M1
taken as written
taken as written
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A claim, beyond doubt, that a zombie is lurching along next to the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without question' reads as 'certainly'; here 'without' has its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters wrap round the question abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozambique is a country in south-east Africa, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Want detective to hold one's drink, in a state

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the drink phrase goes between the two outer words

blocks.note: to miss something is to want or lack it
PI is a private investigator
one is I, and the apostrophe S gives S
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A detective, wanting a drink, ends up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like drunkenness, but 'a state' is the US one, and 'in' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Mississippi is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Underwear found in special shopping centres

blocks.note: S is a standard abbreviation for special
malls are shopping centres

explanation.surface: Underwear on sale in particular shopping centres.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British informal for underwear, the small items in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang smalls are items of underclothing such as pants and socks.

clue.text: A résumé may describe the way to reach a certain standard!

linkWords: A résumé may describe the way to

blocks.clueFragment: A résumé may describe the way
blocks.note: surface reading: a CV sets out the route to meeting the requirements for a job
setter's reading: the letters of 'a resume' are a mixed-up version of a seven-letter word, and the two-letter word after it in the answer serves as the jumble signal

explanation.surface: A CV shows how you meet the job's required standard.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read cryptically, MEASURE UP means MEASURE mixed up, which is how A RESUME is made. The exclamation mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure up is an idiom for being good enough, meeting the expected level.

clue.text: Living ruler relinquishes power

indicators.note: the ruler relinquishes, or gives up, one letter, which is dropped

blocks.note: a president is a head of state
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A head of state still alive gives up his power.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESIDENT loses its P to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Resident as an adjective means living or dwelling in a particular place.

clue.text: In truth, a group of soldiers is returning for plastic surgery

indicators.note: 'in' places the soldiers' word inside the word for truth
something returning goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a fact is a truth
a file is a line of soldiers one behind another

explanation.surface: Truthfully, a troop of soldiers comes back home for cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In truth' reads as 'actually'; here 'In' is the container instruction and 'truth' the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a cosmetic operation that tightens facial skin, a common form of plastic surgery.

clue.text: Drug given by doctor people willingly take

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
a race is a people or ethnic group

explanation.surface: A drug prescribed by a doctor that patients are happy to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or offer is to accept it eagerly.

clue.text: Flying creature rises over the water in French picture

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the creature's name goes backwards
in a down clue one part placed over another sits above it, coming first

blocks.note: a bat is a flying mammal
l'eau is French for the water

explanation.surface: A bat flies up over the water in a French painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or group, a striking picture.

clue.text: Confine one after the other, say

indicators.note: 'say' means as spoken, so the phrase counts by its sound

blocks.note: doing things one after the other is doing them in turn

explanation.surface: Locking people up one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to detain someone, typically in wartime, without trial, so to confine them.

clue.text: Road not damaged in storm

indicators.note: a damaged thing is broken up, so these letters come apart and are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road that came through the storm unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the road was not damaged; the anagram signal 'damaged' sits right beside the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, the most destructive kind of storm.

clue.text: B&B I overcharge to reserve - book in? Refuse to go here!

indicators.note: to reserve is to hold back and keep, so the overcharge word keeps the guesthouse letters inside it

blocks.note: rush is informal for charging someone too much
the letters taken as written, ampersand dropped
B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guest grumbles that the B&B charges too much to make a booking; they refuse to stay there!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse to go here!' reads as a refusal to stay; refuse is the noun, meaning waste. Rush, for overcharge, is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish bin is the container where waste, or refuse, is put.

clue.text: Jack perhaps sent back portion of unsavoury burrito

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the letters come from within the words that follow
sent back means returned the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone sends back part of a nasty-tasting burrito.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ruby was the man who shot Lee Harvey Oswald in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ruby is a famous bearer of the surname, so Jack is an example given with 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Contradict most of religious doctrine

indicators.note: most of means all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a belief is a religious tenet or doctrine

explanation.surface: Disputing nearly all of a church's teachings.
explanation.walkthrough: BELIEF minus its final F.
explanation.definitionFit: To belie is to show something to be false, so to contradict it.

clue.text: Update about America received by Vice President

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so the country letters go inside the title abbreviation

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
VP is the standard abbreviation
AM is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A briefing on America handed to the Vice President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Update' looks like the briefing itself, a noun; it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or overhaul something, giving it a new look, so to update it.

clue.text: Nurse draws intestines

blocks.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
to trail something is to draw or drag it behind

explanation.surface: A nurse pulling out a patient's guts.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the internal organs, especially the bowels or guts.

clue.text: That thing's at first oddly ignored

definitions.note: 'tis is a contraction of 'it is', as 'that thing's' is of 'that thing is'

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Something at first was strangely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like 'initially', but it is the source of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Tis is the poetic contraction of 'it is', and 'that thing's' is likewise a pronoun plus is.

clue.text: Pioneer scouts travelling around rock

indicators.note: travelling around means moving about, so these letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Early explorers making their way round a large rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a boulder; it is slang for a gem, such as a diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is slang for a gemstone, especially a diamond, which is a precious stone.
